    - Much of a node's meaning lives in its **page references** — the `[[double-bracketed]]` links within its content blocks. These connect nodes to the Functions, Flows, Projects, Sources, and UserPilots that give them context. <roam uid="U28zLlsXL"/>
    - When reading a node, expand or follow its page references to understand **why** it exists and **what** it connects to. For example, a Result node's title includes its Source (e.g., `[[RES]] - users synthesized 3x more claims - [[@pilotStudy2025]]`), and its body may reference the Function or Flow it relates to. <roam uid="BQMJ8e_-z"/>
    - **Linked references** (at the bottom of any page) show every block in the graph that mentions that page. This is the primary way to see how a node is used in context — meeting notes, update logs, other discourse nodes, and daily notes entries. <roam uid="G9z0oYOKm"/>
    - **Block references** work similarly for individual blocks (bullets). If a block has a reference count, it has been cited elsewhere. <roam uid="Dcv_AHP0W"/>
  - Search strategies <roam uid="uDgL2s89Q" heading="3"/>
    - Search for discourse nodes by their type prefix: `[[QUE]] -`, `[[ISS]] -`, `[[FLO]] -`, `[[RES]] -`, etc. <roam uid="z9FqVtbYA"/>
    - Search for candidate nodes by their tag: `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`, `#hyp-candidate`, `#clm-candidate`, `#flow-candidate`, `#up-candidate`, `#pro-candidate`. <roam uid="R6ZQgo7E-"/>
    - Search with empty query to see recently edited and viewed content — useful for understanding current activity. <roam uid="aHXgbk2iE"/>
    - For attributes with constrained values (status fields, priorities, tools, etc.), refer to [[roam/js/attribute-select]] for the canonical set of options. <roam uid="MaJPh5WXZ"/>
  - Understanding overall workflows <roam uid="3Qe0kZwzj" heading="3"/>
    - An observation from a pilot (Result) often triggers an idea for improvement (Issue). Issues are higher priority when they improve an important Flow, which in turn enables a key Function. Once engineering works on an issue, it becomes a feature (Artifact). <roam uid="E-6z55uoF"/>
    - Result → Issue → Flow → Function → Artifact traces the path from observation to shipped feature. <roam uid="gFNP0A0S9"/>
- Writing into the graph <roam uid="a7uWA6zlm" heading="2"/>
  - Leave node creation and tagging to the team by default (see **Agent Behavior → General rules** below). When you are explicitly asked to capture something — a candidate node, a pilot observation, a flow — follow these conventions so each block reads cleanly now **and** is trivial to promote into a formal discourse node later. <roam uid="mebOIP95I"/>
  - Put each concept in its own block <roam uid="F3EVfNmD7" heading="3"/>
    - Write one idea — one claim, observation, pain point, flow, or action — per block. Don't pack several into a single bullet. Be parsimonious with any commentary you consider adding. <roam uid="1LMq1Ui6Y"/>
      - Atomic blocks are individually addressable: each can be block-referenced (`((uid))`), tagged, and promoted to a node on its own. A compound bullet can't. <roam uid="rLZacptHP"/>
    - Use indentation to carry structure: the parent block states the idea; child blocks hold its detail, caveats, steps, and references. <roam uid="VFcltIeP4"/>
      - This mirrors a discourse node, where the title is the idea and the template sections are the children. <roam uid="dv7_tHNg5"/>
  - Make candidate blocks formalizable <roam uid="t62zcsYxS" heading="3"/>
    - When you tag a block with a candidate tag, write the statement so it can become the node's **title almost verbatim** — the eventual node title should be roughly the same words as the block. Keep it atomic and self-contained: understandable without the surrounding meeting / log context. <roam uid="QcHWU8FCu"/>
    - Match the target node's title grammar so promotion is mechanical. The candidate tags in use here are `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`, `#hyp-candidate`, `#clm-candidate`, `#flow-candidate`, `#up-candidate`, `#pro-candidate` — each maps to the node type of the same prefix (see **Graph Ontology** above for every format). Common cases: <roam uid="vNFJ3JbII"/>
      - `#res-candidate` → a discrete, past-tense pilot observation → `[[RES]] - {statement} - {Source}`. Name the `@source` / UserPilot in a child so it can be appended to the title on promotion. <roam uid="Xx5QnpXMw"/>
        - Example: `Pilot users created 3x more claims after the canvas node preview shipped #res-candidate` <roam uid="8RsFzOBwL"/>
      - `#iss-candidate` → an actionable dev or research item → `[[ISS]] - {statement}`. <roam uid="0tM9FtTCr"/>
        - Example: `Group nodes on the canvas by semantic similarity #iss-candidate` <roam uid="b8CJepmiH"/>
      - `#flow-candidate` → a tool-specific interaction flow → `[[FLO]] - {statement}`. <roam uid="alG4QCDR4"/>
        - Example: `Preview / view DG node info while on the tldraw canvas #flow-candidate` <roam uid="skG-2mzeZ"/>
    - If you can't yet phrase an idea atomically, leave it as plain text and don't tag it — a vague stub can't be promoted without a rewrite. <roam uid="znTpKgzZv"/>
  - Put supporting context in child blocks <roam uid="YE6FUcUKB" heading="3"/>
    - Everything that explains, grounds, or qualifies a candidate goes in **child blocks beneath it, never crammed into the statement**.  On promotion these children carry over into the node's template sections. <roam uid="VwHNAB0ij"/>
    - `#res-candidate` → Source + method + a screenshot or Loom → **Grounding Context** and **Snippets**. `#flow-candidate` → **Description** (Goal, Loom), **Steps**, **Pain points**. `#iss-candidate` → why it matters + the Flow / Function it improves → Issue Status / Type / Project / Flow properties. <roam uid="-zzjS0GNH"/>
    - Link related nodes with `[[…]]` inside the children — those page references become the node's discourse connections (Supports / Opposes / Informs / Resolves) once it is formalized. <roam uid="pM5ojIoXO"/>
  - Reuse the existing syntax and formatting conventions <roam uid="MEWdJCUaQ" heading="3"/>
    - For how to __reference__ nodes when writing (Roam alias syntax, `((uid))`), follow **Agent Behavior → Citing and referencing nodes** below — don't paste full URLs inside Roam. <roam uid="iqnB7VJ1X"/>
    - For callouts, colors, and foldable blocks, use the palette documented in **Agent Behavior → Formatting** below. <roam uid="1-PwVXvKX"/>
    - Reference only node titles you have actually found in the graph; never fabricate one. Preserve node title regex formats exactly (`[[RES]] - … - {Source}`, `[[FLO]] - …`, `UserPilot/…`) — a malformed title silently drops the block out of the discourse graph. <roam uid="ldsx0Q1Nj"/>
- Agent Behavior <roam uid="HQkVaTtF9" heading="2"/>
  - Information hierarchy <roam uid="Omx-xxku_" heading="3"/>
    - **Prioritize formalized node pages** (full `[[TYPE]] - title` pages with templates filled in). These represent the team's vetted, structured knowledge. <roam uid="gSd5Imn_Z"/>
    - **Then candidate nodes** (`#type-candidate` tagged blocks). These are preliminary but intentionally captured ideas. <roam uid="KPWTNgy6Z"/>
    - **Then remaining content** (meeting notes, daily notes, log entries, comments). These provide context but are less curated. <roam uid="7FBUcDopw"/>
    - Rank by formality, but check authorship before you cite — only human-written blocks are citable. See **Synthesize human content, not agent content** below. <roam uid="RgZPUYxXj" refs="1"/>
  - Synthesize human content, not agent content <roam uid="IxsMpHOOT" heading="3" refs="1"/>
    - **Your job is synthesis of what the team's people wrote.**  Building on agent-authored content closes a loop where agents cite agents and the graph fills with its own echo. <roam uid="2vCRnvaM-" refs="1"/>
    - **This includes your own prior output.** Never cite, quote, count, or treat as evidence a block that you or another agent wrote, in this graph or any other. <roam uid="r-7VcjnUB" refs="1"/>
  - Provenance: who wrote this block <roam uid="psNqP1Ow4" heading="3" refs="1"/>
    - **Never ascribe a statement to a person without querying the block's creator.** Position in the outline, a nearby name, and a `#[[Name]]` tag are not authorship signals — a person tag usually marks an assignee or a mention, and meeting notes are typed by one scribe on everyone's behalf. Look up `:create/user` before writing "X thinks", "per Joel", or any attributed quote. <roam uid="QowkWQTjg" refs="1"/>
    - **When creator and last editor differ, report both.** "Created by `matt-AI-bot`, last edited by Karola Kirsanow" is the honest form. Don't collapse it to one name. <roam uid="ABeXcABpE" refs="1"/>
    - **Speaker initials in meeting notes are the exception, and you should honor them.** On `Sync /` pages, `JC:`, `MAP:`, `MG:`, `KK:`, `MA:` are the scribe's record of who spoke. Attribute the __position__ to the initials and the __block__ to its creator, and say the initials are your basis. <roam uid="zgFhSiYI6" refs="1"/>
    - **If you can't resolve authorship, say the block is unattributed.** Never assign it to the nearest name on the page. <roam uid="CFgMF_i0-" refs="1"/>
    - **Non-human identities in this graph today:** `matt-AI-bot`, `ai-cybrarian`, `cybrarian-ai`, `Michael Gartner (AI)`, and every identity whose display name begins with `API Token:` or `Local API Token:`. Treat those as machine-written unless you have checked otherwise. Per-bot users are still being sorted out — see [[Convention/Human-AI interaction in Roam]]. <roam uid="78YnS6gEC" refs="1"/>
      - A token is not automatically an agent. `API Token: Raycast matt` and `API Token: send2graph` forward text a human typed. Token-created means __provenance unclear__, not __AI-generated__ — report which one you actually found. <roam uid="VBVOklCV1" refs="1"/>
      - `Discourse Graphs`, `Anonymous`, and `Anonymous_1`–`Anonymous_3` are shared or unresolved accounts. Don't attribute their blocks to any individual. <roam uid="rHnvdFRhH" refs="1"/>

  - Citing and referencing nodes <roam uid="1Q-QuB4hm" heading="3"/>

      - `[the grouping issue]([[[[ISS]] - group nodes on the canvas, eg by semantic similarity]])` <roam uid="huKrbfYiZ"/>
    - For block-level references, use the `((uid))` syntax when you have a specific block UID. <roam uid="P03iIKmxK"/>
    - Always include enough of the node title for the reader to understand the reference without clicking through. <roam uid="6rl43A8ym"/>
  - Citing dates <roam uid="FNMHIgv1c" heading="3"/>
    - The team uses the linked references of daily notes pages as a "table of contents" to monitor the team's work that week. Therefore, be judicious in how many times you reference a daily note with wikilinks. The top-level entry usually includes a reference to today's date, and any clear deadline can be referenced once per entry. Other dates should be labeled like `July 29` rather than with wikilinks. <roam uid="AJ-MJrH7M"/>
  - Reading nodes thoroughly <roam uid="UJfOc9mSn" heading="3"/>

    - All the firebase links are public links to images.  Usually, these images are very informative, so for relevant nodes and pages you should open the images and interpret them with your image recognition capabilities <roam uid="EIquKiNkw"/>

# roam/agent guidelines <roam uid="XcDxM3AGm" refs="9"/>

- This is the **discourse-graphs team graph** (dg-team). It tracks product development, user research, and design knowledge for the Discourse Graphs project. Start orientation at [[🚪 Discourse graphs front page for team members]]. <roam uid="ZyEFQdPzy"/>
- Graph Ontology <roam uid="CkMv_I9Hu" heading="2"/>
  - This graph uses a discourse graph node grammar with typed nodes. Each node type has a title format that the Roam plugin uses for identification via regex. Nodes exist at two levels of formality: <roam uid="JZ-ERybz9"/>
    - **Full node pages** — titled with the type prefix (e.g., `[[ISS]] - description`). These are the primary knowledge units. <roam uid="Lr2QOC061"/>
    - **Candidate nodes** — blocks tagged with a candidate hashtag (e.g., `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`). These are seedling ideas not yet promoted to full pages. <roam uid="IxTd36BlH"/>
  - Node Types: Knowledge <roam uid="iJARoph1H" heading="3"/>
    - **Question (QUE)** — the unknowns being explored through pilots and research. Format: `[[QUE]] - {content}`. Sections: Summary, Notes, Testable hypotheses, Snippets. <roam uid="9uXF_YcQQ"/>
    - **Hypothesis (HYP)** — proposed answers to questions; collect evidence for or against. Format: `[[HYP]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#hyp-candidate`. Sections: Rationale, Snippets, Requests for Experiments. <roam uid="jA0VLkwMY"/>
    - **Result (RES)** — a discrete observation from ongoing research, in past tense. Format: `[[RES]] - {content} - {Source}`. Candidate tag: `#res-candidate`. Sections: Summary, Grounding Context, Snippets. Properties: NodeFormality (Draft → ReadyForInternal → ReadyToShare → Published), Contributors. <roam uid="21s0GTu6p"/>
    - **Evidence (EVD)** — a discrete observation from a published dataset or experiment. Format: `[[EVD]] - {content} - {Source}`. Sections: Evidence Description, Snippets, Grounding Context, Centrality slider. <roam uid="zgYL5nVb4"/>
    - **Claim (CLM)** — an assertion about how discourse graphs work or should work. Format: `[[CLM]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#clm-candidate`. <roam uid="9SOQK_533"/>
    - **Source (SRC)** — a referenced publication or external resource. Format: `@{content}`. <roam uid="wenbahwqN"/>
    - **Theory (THE)** — a theoretical framework or model. Format: `[[THE]] - {content}`. <roam uid="UtoPH2BxJ"/>
  - Node Types: Product & UX <roam uid="e-gV24nNQ" heading="3"/>
    - **Function (FUN)** — a UX "use case": a specific situation where Discourse Graphs can be used to enhance the experience. Tool-agnostic in framing, but tied to a concrete user goal. Format: `[[FUN]] - {content}`. Properties: FunctionImportance, FunctionScoping. <roam uid="LjYlqRpUR"/>
    - **Flow (FLO)** — a set of interactions the user performs to accomplish a goal within a particular implementation of Discourse Graphs (Obsidian plugin, Roam plugin, tldraw, etc.). A Flow is the tool-specific instantiation of a Function/Use Case. Format: `[[FLO]] - {content}`. Sections: Description (Goal, Loom, brief description), Steps (Normal flow, Alt flows, Exceptions), Examples, Pain points. Properties: FlowStatus (💭 Hypothetical → 🗓️ Planned → 🤔 Experimental → 🚧 Bespoke → 🔨 Alpha → 🚀 Beta), FlowFrequency, FlowImpact. <roam uid="SVcbz9E3i"/>
    - **Artifact (ART)** — the features, workflows, and UI components we build to enable Flows and Use Cases (Functions). Parts of a system are prefixed with the system name (e.g., `[[ART]] - Roam DG/Query`). Format: `[[ART]] - {content}`. Properties: ArtifactType (Feature/Component or Workflow/Template), ArtStatus (🤔 Prospective → 🖇️ Bespoke → 🧪 Alpha → 🎯 Beta → 💎 Release → 🌐 External). <roam uid="71FJwPgwi"/>
    - **PainPoint (PAI)** — problems, friction, and bottlenecks in user experience. Format: `[[PAI]] - {content}`. Properties: Activity, Function, Flow, UserTool. <roam uid="zD3lBBh9A"/>
    - **Journey (JOU)** — a user journey across multiple functions/flows. Format: `[[JOU]] - {content}`. Sections: Description, Phases, Pain points, Notes. <roam uid="YmhUG6VJX"/>
    - **Activity (ACT)** — an action the user performs that is not specific to any particular tool or method (e.g., "synthesize literature," "discuss findings"). Activities sit upstream of tool-bound Flows and Use Cases. Format: `[[ACT]] - {content}`. <roam uid="1NcVa1g2X"/>
    - **UserPilot** — a specific user or pilot engagement. Format: `UserPilot/{content}`. Properties: User status, UserTool (Roam, Obsidian, Notion, tldraw), UserType (Alpha/Beta/Normie), Lead. <roam uid="5XUZyDshG"/>
    - **CaseStudy (CAS)** — a documented case study. Format: `[[CAS]] - {content}`. <roam uid="ceCyzY2Ei"/>
  - Node Types: Project Management <roam uid="L4Lo_4B1w" heading="3"/>
    - **Issue (ISS)** — a potential action item for development or research. Format: `[[ISS]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#iss-candidate`. Properties: Issue Status (🤔 Considering → 🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → 💬 Awaiting Feedback → ➡ Sent To Linear → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Issue Type (🗳️ Feature Request, 📄 Template improvement, 🐞 Bug Report, 🔬 Research, 🏗️ DG team, 🛠️ Maintenance), Priority, Project, Function, Flow, Lead. <roam uid="jzczOjTM1"/>
    - **Project** — a research or development project. Format: `Project/{content}`. Properties: Project Status (🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Priority. <roam uid="IwUFa4By7"/>
    - **Milestone** — a time-boxed delivery target. Format: `Milestone/{content}`. Properties: Milestone Status, Start/End Date, Priority. <roam uid="NCfJPwcoO"/>
  - Relation Types <roam uid="PZxB_Lim1" heading="3"/>
    - **Supports / Supported By** — Evidence or Result supports a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="QLrw6Cikm"/>
    - **Opposes / Opposed By** — Evidence or Result contradicts a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="RdGHvBjvu"/>
    - **Informs / Informed By** — Evidence, Result, or Claim informs a Question or Hypothesis; Question informs Hypothesis; Hypothesis informs Issue <roam uid="0TFxQSHzV"/>
    - **Reproduces / Reproduced By** — Evidence confirms other Evidence <roam uid="lZNpV65LF"/>
    - **Resolves / Is resolved by** — Result resolves an Issue <roam uid="BKCUPTVYB"/>

Reach for the **`discourse`** server whenever a task depends on the discourse-node / relation grammar (typed nodes, typed relations, the ontology); use the **`roam`** server for general text search, reading arbitrary pages, and all writes. <roam uid="v7YWcac84"/>

Found it — that's the triage template (Need / Fit and urgency / Triage). Drafting the scope expansion against it.

Note it goes into **Notes as a proposal**, so I'd leave `Done When` untouched until you accept it — otherwise the ticket asserts the expansion rather than proposing it.

---

**Proposed scope expansion: per-direction asset size caps**

- **Need**
  - Engineers implementing ENG-1870 (publish) and ENG-2218 (import) each need to know what "too large" means before either can skip anything, and nothing currently defines it. Users are affected downstream: an oversized asset should degrade visibly rather than fail its node.
  - Evidence: the `cross-app-assets` spec has the scenario "Asset exceeds the configured size limit", which has no referent without a number; the design's risk register records that both directions need an explicit cap and that neither may inherit one; and Obsidian's publisher currently enforces a bare `6 * 1024 * 1024` with no name (`syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts`).
- **Fit and urgency**
  - Addresses a need this ticket's Solution already names — it lists "missing, oversized, unsupported and no-row behaviors" as what the shape must carry. Defining the term is contract work; enforcing it is implementation work.
  - Relevant well within six months: ENG-1870 and ENG-2218 are in the current cycle and both read a cap.
  - Why now — whichever of those two ships first would pick the number and the second would inherit it. That is exactly the inheritance [Decision 9](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/Ex0HuOqBS) forbids, reintroduced by the ticket split rather than by anyone deciding it. content.text:
**Task 2.1 complete. Progress: 5/20.**

Two new files in `apps/roam/src/utils/` — platform-specific detection, kept out of the shared contract as ENG-1864's Out of Scope requires.

**`findAssetReferences.ts`** returns the Roam-hosted assets a node's `full` markdown references, deduplicated, in order of first appearance. Two decisions worth your eye:

- **One combined regex, matched in a single pass**, with the five forms in priority order: `![](url)`, `{{[[pdf|audio|video]]: url}}`, `{{pdf|audio|video: url}}`, `[label](url)`, then a bare URL. A single pass is what makes "don't count the URL inside an embed as a bare URL too" fall out for free rather than needing bookkeeping. I added the bracket-less `{{pdf: url}}` form since Roam accepts both, and the plain-link form since a *linked* rather than embedded upload is still an asset — Decision 4 depends on that, since it's the case that needs a label on import.
- **`isRoamStorageUrl` matches host plus bucket, not the path shape.** Every Roam upload lands in `firescript-577a2.appspot.com`; the `imgs/app/<graph>/<uid>` path is Roam's to change. Parsing with `URL` rather than a substring test also rejects a lookalike host like `firebasestorage.googleapis.com.evil.test`, which a naive `includes` would accept — there's a test for it.

External references are excluded, which is the spec's "a resource that was never an asset of the node": a hotlinked image, a DOI link, a Roam page URL. We can't fetch someone else's bytes and shouldn't store them.

**15 tests** covering the four cases the task names plus the extra embed forms we agreed to: each of the five forms, external-link exclusion, mixed content, dedup across different forms, no double-counting inside embeds, trailing sentence punctuation after a bare URL, empty input, and four `isRoamStorageUrl` cases.

Full Roam suite is 179/179 across 26 files; `check-types`, `eslint`, `prettier` clean.

Next is 2.2 — fetching one referenced asset from Roam storage and resolving its original name from the object descriptor, with the `metadata["file-name"]` present/absent cases. That's the first code that talks to Firebase, and per the design it reads the descriptor by *stripping* `alt=media`, which is cheap and bypasses the Roam API entirely.

Let's back up one step. Here's a finding from the code review:
- packages/database/src/crossAppContracts.ts:84 — Contract/implementation mismatch on reference. The contract says it is "the token exactly as the node's full content expresses it… a vault path on a platform that addresses assets by path," mapping to FileReference.filepath. The only existing publisher of that column, syncPublishedNodeAssets at apps/obsidian/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:748 (fname: attachment.path), stores the resolved path from getFirstLinkpathDest, not the literal token. Obsidian's default link setting is shortest-path, so a note containing ![[rem-sleep-recall.png]] publishes filepath = "attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png"; a destination matching content tokens against reference finds no entry and leaves the embed unresolved. The new Obsidian example at crossAppNodeContract.example.ts:73 writes the embed with its full path, which is not the common Obsidian form, so the fixture hides this. Either the contract states reference is the resolved path (and destinations resolve before matching), or the publisher stores the raw token.
It seems like a real problem. But I think we tested this in Obsidian; do we expand paths to match while looking for matches in imported markdown?

Yes — Obsidian expands paths, and that's why the predicted failure doesn't occur there. The finding is still worth acting on, but its real bite is elsewhere. Evidence:

**The download never consults the markdown.** `importAssetsForNode` fetches `my_file_references` rows for the node and downloads each by `filehash` (`importNodes.ts:459-489`). The bytes land in the vault regardless of what tokens the content holds.

**Link resolution tries Obsidian's own resolver first.** In `resolveFilePath` (`importNodes.ts:658-670`), the first attempt is `findImportedAssetFile(path)`, which calls `app.metadataCache.getFirstLinkpathDest(linkPath, targetFile.path)` and then checks the result is one of the files just written (`newPaths`). Only if that misses does it fall back to `getNewPathForLink`, the `pathMapping` string lookup. So `![[rem-sleep-recall.png]]` resolves through Obsidian's shortest-path rules to the imported asset, and never needs to string-match `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png`.

So finding's premise is right and its consequence is wrong — **for Obsidian**. Three things remain true and worth fixing:

1. **The contract comment is factually wrong.** `reference` is not "the token exactly as the content expresses it" for a path-addressed platform; `syncPublishedNodeAssets` stores `attachment.path`, the resolved path from `getFirstLinkpathDest`. The comment should say `reference` is the source's own *address* for the asset, and that a destination resolves a content token to it using the source platform's addressing rules — exact match for URL-addressed sources, path resolution for path-addressed ones.

2. **The real exposure is the Roam importer, task 5.1.** Roam has no vault and no `getFirstLinkpathDest`. An Obsidian-origin node whose markdown says `![[rem-sleep-recall.png]]` against a row saying `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` cannot be matched by the equality rule 5.1 is currently specified with ("resolve each reference through its recorded row, leaving a token unchanged only when no row matches"). That's unwritten code, so this is a design constraint to record now rather than a bug to fix now. The workable rule: exact match, else unique trailing-path-segment match, else leave the token — which stays inside the existing degradation path.

3. **The fixture hides it, as the review says.** I wrote the Obsidian embed with its full path, which isn't the common Obsidian form. Changing it to `![[rem-sleep-recall.png]]` while `reference` stays `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` makes the mismatch visible and forces 5.1 to confront it.

I'd **not** change the publisher to store the raw token, which is the finding's other option. `filepath` is a primary-key component; the raw token is not unique per asset (two notes can embed the same file under different link forms), and the Obsidian importer's `pathMapping` fallback is keyed vault-relative, so it would lose its fallback.

Want me to make those three changes — contract comment, fixture, and a design note pinning 5.1's matching rule? That's a revision to 1.3's output plus a design edit to mirror, so it interrupts 2.2.

Checked, and it's more tractable than it looks.

**The token is available at both call sites, and they're identical.** `publishNode.ts:445` and `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:695` both do the same map — `embeds.map(({ link }) => getFirstLinkpathDest(link, file.path))` — discarding `link` and keeping only the `TFile`. So the raw token isn't lost upstream, it's dropped in two copies of the same two lines. The change is to carry `{ token, file }` pairs instead of `TFile[]`, which is also a chance to extract that duplicated mapping into one helper.

**Your uniqueness argument holds.** The PK is `(source_local_id, space_id, filepath)`, and `source_local_id` *is* the document. A token resolves to exactly one file within a note, so it's unique where the key needs it to be. The pathological case — one note embedding the same asset under two different link forms — yields two rows sharing a `filehash`, which is already what `addFile` is built for: one blob, N references. No new problem.

**On the migration: I think it's cheaper than it sounds — no SQL backfill.** `syncPublishedNodeAssets` already deletes rows whose `filepath` isn't in the current set and inserts what's missing. After the change, a node's next asset sync computes tokens, misses the old resolved-path rows on lookup, inserts token rows, and the existing cleanup deletes the stale ones. The blob is untouched because `file_exists` short-circuits the upload. **So it self-heals per node on the next sync**, and a SQL backfill isn't possible anyway — reconstructing the original token needs the vault, not the database.

The interim state is the documented degradation: an already-published node not yet re-synced has resolved-path rows, so a Roam import of it fails to match and leaves the token in place. Obsidian import is unaffected either way, since it resolves through `getFirstLinkpathDest` first.

Two consequences worth deciding on before this lands:

1. **Imported assets may lose their folder nesting in Obsidian→Obsidian import.** The importer derives its target path by decomposing `filepath` (`importNodes.ts:896-901`). Today that's `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png`; with a shortest-path token it's just `rem-sleep-recall.png`. That's task 3.1's territory and it changes existing behavior, so 3.1 should confront it rather than discover it.
2. **This makes 5.1 pure string equality**, which is the whole point — no Obsidian knowledge in the Roam importer, and the contract comment I was about to weaken becomes literally true as written.

It's an Obsidian publisher change, so it isn't ENG-1864. **ENG-1871** ("Validate Obsidian published-node asset output for cross-app import") looks like the natural home — this is precisely its subject — though it's currently scoped as validation, so it'd need the same kind of scope-expansion note we just wrote, or a new ticket blocking ENG-1870.

content.text:
Partly — and the mechanism you're describing already exists, which sharpens the fork rather than dissolving it.

**The field is real and already used.** `upsertNodesAsContentWithEmbeddings.ts:67` publishes `metadata: { filePath: node.file.path }`, and the importer reads it as `originalNodePath`, using it at `importNodes.ts:589-591` — `getCanonicalFromOriginalNote` joins the source note's directory to the link. So "resolve a token against the source note's location" is implemented today, as the third fallback in `getNewPathForLink`.

**But it only covers two of Obsidian's three link settings.** Obsidian resolves a token according to the vault's "New link format":

| Setting | Token for the fixture | Computable from `filePath`? |
|---|---|---|
| Absolute path in vault | `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` | Yes — equality |
| Relative path to file | `./attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` | Yes — join note dir, already implemented |
| **Shortest path when possible** (default) | `rem-sleep-recall.png` | **No** |

Shortest-path is the default and the case the finding raises. Resolving it means searching the whole vault for a file with that basename — that's what `getFirstLinkpathDest` does, and it's why the Obsidian importer works. It is not derivable from the note's path: `notes/sleep.md` + `rem-sleep-recall.png` gives you `notes/rem-sleep-recall.png`, and the asset is in `attachments/`. The note's location tells you nothing about where the asset lives.

So `filePath` shrinks the gap but doesn't close it. The choice is unchanged in kind:

- **(a) Publisher stores the raw token.** Every destination matches by equality, forever, one rule. Costs the `{token, file}` threading, heal-on-resync, and 3.1 confronting the folder-nesting change.
- **(b) Destinations resolve.** No publisher change, no migration — but the Roam importer needs three matching modes (equality, note-dir join, basename suffix) and can't know which setting produced a given token, so it must try all three and pick. That is provenance-specific behavior living in the consumer, which is what you objected to, and `filePath` reduces it from three unknowns to one rather than removing it.

I still favour (a), now for a tighter reason than before: under (b) the ambiguity is permanent and unfixable from the destination side — two assets in one node sharing a basename cannot be disambiguated by any rule the Roam importer could apply — whereas (a) makes the reference exact at the only point where the truth is actually known, which is the publisher standing in the vault.

Worth noting (b) is not free of migration either: it doesn't need one *now*, but if the rule ever proves insufficient you're migrating then, with more published rows.

content.text:
Good instinct, and checking the importer makes it work — but the assignments have to go the opposite way round from the obvious one.

**First, the resolved path does have a consumer.** `importNodes.ts:895-906` feeds `filepath` to `getAssetPathRelativeToNote(filepath, originalNodePath)`, then writes to `import/{space}/{that}`, creating parent folders. So the directory part reproduces the source's layout in the destination vault. My option (a) would flatten that for shortest-path tokens — a real behavior loss I'd been treating as hypothetical.

**The obvious two-field split doesn't work.** Putting the token in `filename` and keeping the resolved path in `filepath` means `filename` holds a token for Obsidian rows and a name for Roam rows. A destination reading it can't tell which, so it's origin-dependent semantics in the consumer — the exact thing we keep refusing.

**Swapping them does work:**

| | `filepath` | `filename` |
|---|---|---|
| meaning | the token as the content expresses it | the name-or-path the source stored it under |
| Roam | the Firebase URL | `CleanShot 2025-11-16 at 17.14.44@2x.png` |
| Obsidian | `rem-sleep-recall.png` | `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` |

Both columns now have **one meaning each, across origins**. `filepath` is uniformly "what content refers to", so 5.1 is string equality with no Obsidian knowledge. `filename` is uniformly "the source's own storage name-or-path", used for local placement — and 3.1's rule survives verbatim, because "decompose `filename` as a path" gives `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` for Obsidian and a bare name for Roam, which decomposes to itself. Folder layout is preserved; nothing in the importer's placement logic changes except which column it reads.

It also makes `filename` non-null far more often, which is the direction Decision 8 wanted anyway — the destination stops inferring and starts reading.

Costs, honestly:

- Same publisher change and same heal-on-resync migration as before — `filepath` still changes meaning for Obsidian rows, so old rows still don't match tokens until a node re-syncs.
- The column called `filename` would sometimes hold a path. That's a naming smell, though the design already plans a post-v0 rename of `filepath` to `source_ref`/`path_or_url`; this makes the pair `source_ref` + `source_path` and the rename more clearly worth doing.
- 3.1 must read `filename` rather than `filepath` for placement, which is a one-line change to a task not yet written.

This is better than either of my earlier options: it keeps every destination origin-agnostic *and* preserves layout. Shall I write it up as a design revision — a new decision plus edits to Decision 8 — and a scope proposal on ENG-1871, before touching code?

content.text:
Here's the write-up against the triage template, unattached to any ticket. I've presented the options rather than only my recommendation, since it's going to group decision.

---

**`CrossAppAsset.reference` says "the content's own token", but the Obsidian publisher stores a resolved vault path**

- **Need**
  - Anyone implementing a destination importer needs one rule for matching a token in shared markdown to a recorded asset reference. Today the contract promises `reference` is "the token exactly as the node's full content expresses it", and for Roam that is true — the token is the Firebase URL. For Obsidian it is not: `syncPublishedNodeAssets` stores `attachment.path`, the *resolved* path from `getFirstLinkpathDest` (`syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:748`).
  - Obsidian's default link setting is "shortest path when possible", so a note containing `![[rem-sleep-recall.png]]` publishes `filepath = "attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png"`. The two strings differ, and nothing records the one the content actually holds.
  - Raised in code review of PR #1392. The Obsidian→Obsidian path is **not** broken: its importer resolves through `getFirstLinkpathDest` first and only falls back to string lookup (`importNodes.ts:658-670`), so it repairs the mismatch using the vault. The exposure is the Roam importer (ENG-2217/ENG-2219), which has no vault and no resolver, and is currently specified to match by equality.
  - The fixture added in PR #1392 hides this: it writes the Obsidian embed with its full path, which is not the common Obsidian form.
- **Fit and urgency**
  - Addresses the project need that a destination resolves assets **by reference, not by origin** — the load-bearing requirement of the `cross-app-assets` spec, and the reason Decision 8 exists.
  - Squarely within six months: ENG-1870, ENG-2217, ENG-2218 and ENG-2219 are in the current cycle, and the Roam link rewriter is the first consumer that will hit it.
  - Why now: every Obsidian node published before a fix carries rows keyed by resolved path. No SQL backfill can repair them — reconstructing the original token needs the vault, not the database — so the cost of delay is measured in published rows, and the fix heals only as nodes re-sync. Deciding after ENG-2217 ships means the Roam importer will already contain whichever workaround it needed.
- **Options**
  - **A — Destination resolves.** No publisher change, no migration. The Roam importer tries equality, then joins the source note's directory (`Content.metadata.filePath`, already published and already used as `originalNodePath`), then matches on trailing path segments. Rejected in discussion: it puts Obsidian's link conventions inside the Roam importer, and the ambiguous case — two assets in one node sharing a basename — is undecidable from the destination side, permanently.
  - **B — Publisher stores the raw token in `filepath`.** Destinations match by equality forever. But the importer feeds `filepath` to `getAssetPathRelativeToNote` to reproduce the source's folder layout under `import/{space}/` (`importNodes.ts:895-906`), so a shortest-path token flattens that layout.
  - **C — Swap the meanings of the two existing columns.** `filepath` holds the token as the content expresses it; `filename` holds the name-or-path the source stored it under. Roam: URL + `CleanShot ….png`. Obsidian: `rem-sleep-recall.png` + `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png`. Each column then has one meaning across origins: matching reads `filepath` by equality, placement decomposes `filename` as a path — a bare name decomposes to itself. Layout is preserved, no new column, and `filename` becomes non-null in the common case, which is the direction Decision 8 already wanted.
- **Cost of C, stated plainly**
  - The Obsidian publisher must carry `{ token, file }` pairs instead of `TFile[]`. Both call sites (`publishNode.ts:445`, `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:695`) already compute the token and discard it in identical two-line maps, so this also removes a duplication.
  - Migration is by re-sync, not by SQL: `syncPublishedNodeAssets` already deletes rows absent from the current set and inserts what is missing, and `file_exists` suppresses a re-upload, so a node heals on its next asset sync. Until then a Roam import of that node leaves tokens unresolved — the documented degradation path, not a break.
  - The column named `filename` would sometimes hold a path. The design already plans a post-v0 rename of `filepath`; this makes the pair `source_ref` + `source_path` and strengthens the case for doing it.
  - The Roam side is unaffected throughout: its token, its URL and its `filepath` are already the same string.
- **Triage**
  - Clear enough to ticket once an option is chosen; the work is small and confined to the Obsidian publisher plus one line in the destination naming rule.
  - Outcome: **Explore** — needs a group decision between A, B and C.
  - Reason: it changes the meaning of a primary-key column and of a field the contract documents, so it should not be settled inside an implementation PR.

---

Two things I'd flag for the group: the choice is really "where does provenance knowledge live" — in the publisher, which stands in the vault and knows the truth, or in every destination forever. And whichever way it goes, the misleading fixture in PR #1392 should be corrected either way, since it currently makes the common Obsidian case invisible.

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.

|---|---|---|

| Relative path to file | `../attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` | `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` |

| `filepath` | `filename` | token in content |
|---|---|---|
| `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` | *(null)* | `rem-sleep-recall.png` |

| `filepath` | `filename` | token in content |
|---|---|---|

Fair. I wrote it for someone who had been in this conversation. Rewriting for a cold reader: a short background, a concrete failure anyone can picture, and no in-house vocabulary. "Token" is gone, replaced by **written path** against **resolved path**, which explains itself.

---

**Which path should we save when an Obsidian note publishes an image?**

**Background**

When a node is published, its images and attachments are copied into shared storage so the other app can show them. Each copied file gets a row in `FileReference` with two relevant columns:

- `filepath`: how we identify the file
- `filename`: the file's original name (added recently, currently null for Obsidian files)

When another app imports the node, it reads the node's markdown, finds each image link, and has to work out which stored file that link refers to. It does that by looking up the link against `filepath`.

**The problem, concretely**

A user has a note `notes/sleep.md` with an image stored at `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png`. They embed it. Obsidian writes this into the note:

```
![[rem-sleep-recall.png]]
```

We publish the node. The row we save is:

```
filepath = "attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png"
filename = null
```

Now Roam imports that node. It reads `rem-sleep-recall.png` from the markdown, looks for a row with that `filepath`, finds nothing, and leaves the link alone. The image does not appear.

The two strings differ because Obsidian shortens links when it writes them, and we save the full path after resolving the link. Obsidian has three settings for how it writes a link, and only one produces a string matching what we save:

| Obsidian "New link format" | Written in the note | We save |
|---|---|---|
| **Shortest path when possible** (default) | `rem-sleep-recall.png` | `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` |
| Relative path to file | `../attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` | `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` |
| Absolute path in vault | `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` | `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` |

The default setting is the one that breaks.

**Why we cannot just fix it in Roam**

Obsidian imports these nodes correctly today, because it asks the vault to resolve the shortened link, the same way it resolves any link (`importNodes.ts:658-670`). Roam has no vault and no equivalent lookup.

To match without a vault, Roam would have to try three strategies in turn, one per Obsidian setting, and it cannot tell which setting produced any given link. It would also fail permanently when one node has two images with the same file name in different folders. That teaches the Roam importer the rules of Obsidian, which is what the shared format exists to avoid.

Roam-published nodes do not have this problem. A Roam image link is a URL, and we save that same URL, so the lookup already matches exactly.

**Options**

Each is shown with the default Obsidian setting, the case that currently fails.

**A. Change nothing. Make each destination resolve shortened links.**

| `filepath` | `filename` | link in the note |
|---|---|---|
| `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` | null | `rem-sleep-recall.png` |

Roam tries an exact match, then joins the note's folder, then matches on file name alone. Two images with the same name in one node stay unresolvable. Every future destination inherits this.

**B. Save the written path in `filepath`.**

| `filepath` | `filename` | link in the note |
|---|---|---|
| `rem-sleep-recall.png` | null | `rem-sleep-recall.png` |

Lookups become exact matches everywhere. But on import into Obsidian we rebuild the source folder structure from `filepath` (`importNodes.ts:895-906`), and a bare file name has no folder, so imported attachments land flat instead of under `attachments/`.

**C. Save both, one per column.**

| origin | `filepath`: what the note links to | `filename`: where the source kept it |
|---|---|---|
| Obsidian | `rem-sleep-recall.png` | `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png` |
| Roam | `https://firebasestorage…/lqP2ioVNC3.png?alt=media&token=…` | `CleanShot 2025-11-16 at 17.14.44@2x.png` |

Each column means the same thing for both apps. Lookups read `filepath` and match exactly. Placement reads `filename` and splits it into folders, and a plain file name splits into itself, so both apps follow one code path. Folder structure is preserved, and no new column is needed.

**What C costs**

- The publisher keeps the written link alongside the resolved file. Both places that build the attachment list (`publishNode.ts:445`, `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:695`) already compute it and then throw it away, in duplicated code.
- No database migration, and none is possible: rebuilding a shortened link needs the vault, not the database. Publishing already deletes rows that no longer apply and inserts the current ones, and the file itself is not re-uploaded, so each node corrects itself the next time it syncs.
- Until a node re-syncs, importing it into Roam leaves its images unresolved, which is the same behavior as today. Importing it into Obsidian is unaffected.
- `filename` would sometimes hold a path rather than a name. We already plan to rename these columns after v0, and this makes better names worth choosing.

**Decision needed**

A, B, or C. It changes the meaning of a primary key column, so it should not be decided inside an implementation PR.

---

Worth deciding once for the group: how much background these proposals should carry by default. This one runs long because it assumes nothing. If your teammates would rather have a three-line summary with the detail folded underneath, I can write it that way instead.

Your lead's summary is right, and the question is a fair one. Let me answer it straight, including where my own write-up overstated things.

**Yes, that's the problem.** Obsidian stores a resolved path, the markdown carries a shortened link, Obsidian repairs the difference with `getFirstLinkpathDest`, and Roam has no such function.

**Fuzzy matching would mostly work.** I should say that plainly rather than defend the proposal. The candidate set is small (just that node's own rows), and when a fuzzy match fails you fall back to today's behavior, which is leaving the link alone. So most of the risk is bounded. Three cases are not:

1. **It can silently rewrite the wrong link.** A note references `attachments/figure.png` as its own asset, and also links to `https://example.com/figure.png`, someone else's image. Basename matching connects the external link to our stored copy, and the importer rewrites it to point at our file. The reader sees the wrong image, and nothing errors. Avoiding this needs a rule like "match URLs only exactly, allow suffix matching only for path-shaped links", which is fine, but it is a rule someone has to think of.

2. **Every destination writes its own version of it.** Roam now, anything later. The rules are small but not obvious, and two implementations that differ slightly will disagree about the same node.

3. **Ambiguity inside one node.** Here I overstated the case earlier and should correct it: Obsidian's "shortest path when possible" only shortens when the name is *unambiguous in the vault*, so it mostly avoids creating this. It can still arise later, when a user adds or moves a file so that a previously unique name stops being unique, since existing links are not rewritten. Rarer than I implied.

**But the `filename` point is a different question, and this is the part I'd push back on.** Fuzzy matching answers "which row does this link refer to". `filename` answers "what should the file be called once I write it into the user's vault". Those don't substitute for each other.

A Roam image link looks like:

```
https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2FMAPLab%2FlqP2ioVNC3.png?alt=media&token=9f1c07a4…
```

Fuzzy matching on part of that URL does find the row. But the only name derivable from the URL is `lqP2ioVNC3.png`, Roam's random storage id. Without `filename`, every Roam image imported into an Obsidian vault is called something like that, forever. Renaming them later breaks links the user has written themselves, so it is close to irreversible. The real name lives in Roam's Firebase metadata (`CleanShot 2025-11-16 at 17.14.44@2x.png`), which the publisher can read cheaply and no destination can.

So the honest summary for your lead:

- Fuzzy matching is a legitimate cheaper option for **matching**. Its cost is a subtle rule, reimplemented per destination, with one silent-failure mode worth guarding.
- It does **not** remove the need for `filename`, because that solves **naming**, not matching. And the column already shipped in ENG-2229, so the open question is only whether the Roam publisher fills it.

If that lands, the decision shrinks usefully: fuzzy match versus option C for matching, and `filename` gets filled either way.

Checked. Two facts that shape the answer:

**ENG-1864 pins semantics, not names.** Its Solution says "the token exactly as the node's content expresses it, the content hash, and an optional original name", and Done When says only that payloads are "documented or typed". So nothing in the ticket fixes a name. The names exist only in the code I wrote: `CrossAppAsset.reference`, `contentHash`, `filename`.

**ENG-2229 is unmerged.** We're on `eng-1864-…`, and `d76bd3f23` (the column) is an ancestor in the stack, not on main. So the `filename` column has never shipped, and renaming it costs an edit to an unmerged migration rather than a second migration later. That window closes when the stack merges.

Those point in different directions for the two columns:

**The new column: worth renaming now.** `source_path` survives all three outcomes. Under C it holds `attachments/rem-sleep-recall.png`; under A or B it holds Roam's original name, which is a path in Roam's flat namespace, so the name isn't wrong there either. And it's honest about the fact that this thing sometimes holds a path, which `filename` actively misleads about. Cost is an edit to an unmerged migration plus a re-review of a small PR.

**`filepath` → `source_ref`: I'd wait.** Not because it's hard, though it's wider than it sounds: 36 references across 12 files, the view's explicit column list, `addFile`'s `fname` parameter, dbTypes regeneration, and both Obsidian call paths. The real reason is that `source_ref` asserts the semantics we're currently arguing about. It means "what the content refers to", which is true under B and C and false under A, where the column keeps holding a resolved path. Renaming it now quietly presumes we win the argument.

Better: if C lands, do the rename and the meaning change in the same migration. One migration where a column changes name and content together reads far more clearly in history than a rename followed weeks later by a semantic change to the same column, which is the kind of pair that misleads whoever reads it in a year.

So my suggestion: rename the unmerged column to `source_path` now if you want the conceptual clarity early, and hold `source_ref` as part of whatever C's migration turns out to be. Want me to prepare the `source_path` change so it's ready if you decide to take it?

Renamed, everything green (59 + 179 tests, both `check-types`, prettier, eslint).

```
reference  → sourceRef
filename   → sourcePath
contentHash  (unchanged)
```

The comments moved with them, and `sourcePath` now describes the C semantics directly: *"Where the source kept the asset: a name on a platform with a flat asset namespace, a path on one with folders. A destination derives the name and placement of its local copy by decomposing this as a path, and a bare name decomposes to itself."* That sentence is doing real work — it's the thing that makes one code path serve both platforms, and it was invisible while the field was called `filename`.

Three notes:

- **`sourcePath` does presume C**, in the sense that under A it would hold only a name and never a path. I went ahead because the cost of being wrong is a two-line edit on a type with no consumers, unlike the column rename where I argued for waiting. Flagging it so the inconsistency is deliberate rather than sloppy.
- I updated the one doc comment in `findAssetReferences.ts` that named the old field.
- The DB columns are untouched: still `filepath` and `filename`. So contract and columns now differ in name, which is fine — they already did (`contentHash` vs `filehash`) — but if C lands, the migration that renames the columns should land `source_ref`/`source_path` so the two vocabularies converge rather than drifting further.

Worth deciding whether ENG-1864's description should record the field names now that they're this deliberate. Its Done When only asks that payloads be "documented or typed", so nothing forces it, but a reviewer arriving at the PR would benefit from the ticket naming the three fields and what each carries. Want me to draft that as a Notes addition?

{"id":"ENG-1870","uuid":"d002b2b0-a243-427d-9395-1ff708a953a5","title":"Copy Roam-origin assets into Supabase on publish","description":"## Problem

* Roam shared-node markdown references files held in Roam's Firebase storage. Nothing puts those bytes where a destination can resolve them the ordinary way, so every destination would have to know about Firebase to use them.
* An asset that cannot be copied must not stop the node from publishing.

## Solution

* After content upsert, find the asset references in the node's `full` markdown, fetch each from Firebase, and pass it to `addFile` with its original filename.
* Leave the markdown unchanged. The Firebase URL stays as the reference token and becomes the row's `filepath`.
* Skip an asset over an explicit size limit, and return failures as part of the publish result.

## Done When

* Publishing a Roam node with an image writes a `FileReference` whose `filepath` is the URL as it appears in the markdown and whose `filename` is the original upload name.
* The published markdown is unchanged by the asset stage.
* An asset that cannot be fetched does not fail the publish, and appears in the result.
* Re-publishing an unchanged node uploads no bytes again.

## Out of Scope

* Rewriting asset links in published markdown. Decision 2 keeps the URL as the reference token.
* Destination-side import. <issue id="c645eb08-5105-4307-a951-81f802b8ea5f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1872/copy-shared-assets-into-roam-on-import">ENG-1872</issue> and its sub-issues cover that.
* Garbage collection of copied bytes. The existing `file_gc` path already handles it.
* Backfilling nodes already published from Roam. Their markdown still holds working URLs, and a worklist is derivable from `Content.text` when one is wanted.

## Notes

* [Decision 2](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/TpIHc4zeb>) on [OpenSpec/CrossApp asset references](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/Ex0HuOqBS>).
* **Ordering: **`FileReference` has a foreign key to `Content`, so this stage runs after `upsert_content`, not alongside it.
* `addFile` already hashes, deduplicates through `file_exists`, uploads, and resolves duplicate keys. This ticket fetches from Firebase and calls it — it reimplements none of that, and needs no registry, because Supabase deduplicates by hash on its own.
* The original filename comes from the Firebase object descriptor: request the storage URL with `alt=media` stripped and read `metadata["file-name"]`. Fall back to the storage uid where that key is absent, as Roam's own `file.get` does.
* Set the size limit in this ticket. It is a different limit from the import side's — what we are willing to pull out of Firebase and store at our cost, not what Roam will accept.
* The earlier criterion "persisted with the node's access scope" holds by construction: a `FileReference` hangs off the node's `Content` row, so it is reachable exactly when the node is. See [Decision 7](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/xlPuc0A6E>).
* **Not split**, unlike <issue id="c645eb08-5105-4307-a951-81f802b8ea5f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1872/copy-shared-assets-into-roam-on-import">ENG-1872</issue>. That direction needed a registry because `file.upload` is not idempotent, and a link rewriter because destination URLs change. Neither applies here.

content.text:
**Task 2.2 complete. Progress: 6/20.** New: `apps/roam/src/utils/fetchRoamAsset.ts` plus 13 tests. Full Roam suite 192/192, everything else clean.

Three functions, split deliberately:

- **`assetDescriptorUrl`** removes `alt=media` and keeps the download token. The token governs access to both the metadata and the bytes, so dropping it would break the descriptor read on a non-public object.
- **`fetchAssetDescriptor`** reads name, mimetype and size without transferring the file. Name resolution is `metadata["file-name"]`, falling back to the storage uid — taken from the descriptor's own `name` field when present, otherwise parsed from the URL. That matches what Roam's own `file.get` does, so an asset with no recorded name gets the same name here as it would there.
- **`fetchRoamAsset`** reads the descriptor, then downloads.

Two things worth your eye, both small judgement calls:

**The descriptor also yields `size`, and I exposed it.** The design notes this read is cheap, and that makes 2.3's cap check possible *before* downloading rather than after — we can decline a 40 MB asset without pulling 40 MB through the browser. The docstring says so, so 2.3 has the option. Slightly beyond a literal reading of 2.2, but it's one field off JSON we're already parsing, and discarding it would be the odd choice.

**`fetchRoamAsset` reports the byte length it actually received, not the descriptor's claim.** Firebase returns `size` as a string, and it's Roam's assertion about the object; once we hold the bytes, `byteLength` is the fact. They should agree, and if they ever don't, the one we trust should be the one we can verify.

On failure: both functions **throw**, with the URL and status in the message. That's deliberate — 2.5 puts the per-asset catch in the publish stage, so the spec's "an asset failure never fails the node" is enforced at the stage boundary rather than smeared across every helper.

Next is 2.3: copy a fetched asset through `addFile` with its `filename`, skipping anything above `MAX_PUBLISHED_ASSET_BYTES`, with the dedup and skip-result tests. That's also where we agreed `addFile` should start returning its content hash.

**Task 2.3 complete. Progress: 7/20.** All suites green: Roam 198, database 60, plus `check-types` in all three packages and eslint/prettier clean.

Four files touched:

**`packages/database/src/lib/files.ts`** — `addFile` now returns the content hash (`Promise<void>` → `Promise<string>`), as we agreed to defer to this task. Additive; the Obsidian caller ignores it. One new test asserts the returned hash matches the stored `filehash`.

**`apps/roam/src/utils/copyAssetToSharedStorage.ts`** — new. Reads the descriptor, decides on the cap, downloads, calls `addFile`, returns a discriminated `copied | skipped` result. It reimplements nothing: hashing, dedup via `file_exists`, and duplicate-key handling stay in `addFile`.

**`apps/roam/src/utils/fetchRoamAsset.ts`** — two additions, both flagged since they touch 2.2's reviewed output:

- **Split out `fetchAssetBytes`.** Without it, this task would read the descriptor, then call `fetchRoamAsset`, which reads the descriptor *again* — two metadata requests per asset. `fetchRoamAsset` now composes the two and is unchanged from the outside.
- **`createdAt` / `modifiedAt` from Firebase's `timeCreated` and `updated`.** `addFile` needs timestamps for the row, and the asset's own are the right ones: they're what Obsidian passes (`attachment.stat.ctime/mtime`), and `last_modified` drives the importer's "is the local copy newer" check. The node's timestamps are the fallback when Firebase reports none.

The decision worth your attention: **the cap is checked from the descriptor first, so an oversized asset's bytes never cross the network.** A 40 MB file is declined after a small JSON read. Where Roam reports no size, the check repeats after download, so the cap always holds. Both paths are tested, including the "no size reported, under cap, copies fine" case.

`skipped` carries `sourcePath`, `size` and `limit`, not just the URL — a user-facing notice in 2.5 can then say the file's name and how far over it was, rather than showing a 200-character storage URL.

content.text:
**Task 2.4 complete. Progress: 8/20.** Roam suite 205/205, `check-types` and prettier clean, no new lint findings.

**New: `apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodeAssets.ts`** — the stage. For each successfully upserted node it reads `content.full.value`, finds the asset references, and copies each. It reads the markdown and never writes it, so publication leaves every link exactly as the page wrote it.

**Changed: `publishNodesToGroups.ts`** — the stage is wired in with two placement constraints, both commented in place:

```ts
// After the content upsert, because FileReference has a foreign key to Content, and
// before the access grants, so a node becomes visible with its assets already recorded.
result.assetResults = await publishNodeAssets({ ... });
```

The "after upsert" half is required: `FileReference` FKs to `Content`. The "before grants" half is a judgement call. Granting first would make a node visible to a group in the window before its assets are recorded, so an import in that window would resolve nothing. Assets first closes that window. It costs a little latency before the grant, and asset failures don't block the grant, so a node still publishes when its assets don't.

It only passes nodes in `upsertedNodeUids`, so a node whose upsert failed gets no asset work and no orphan rows.

`PublishNodesResult` gains `assetResults`. Populating it is this task; **surfacing it is 2.5**, which is where the reporting shape gets decided.

One thing that belongs to 2.5 but I put here anyway: the per-asset `try/catch`. Without it, this task would have introduced a path where one unreachable image throws out of `publishNodesToGroups` and takes the publish with it. Adding the stage and leaving that open for a task wasn't defensible, so failures are captured as `{ status: "failed", … }` from the start. 2.5 decides what's done with them.

Seven tests: the recorded `filepath` is the URL from the markdown, the markdown is unchanged afterwards, a node with no assets records nothing, a node with no `full` content is skipped, an unfetchable asset becomes a failure rather than a throw, an over-cap asset becomes a skip, and each result is attributed to the node that referenced it.
